consumer: The frontend map renderer that paints ground items per tile, asking 'what items would the GUI actually DISPLAY on this tile for the avatar right now?'
scope: The visibility/memory-filtered view of each tile's items as the GUI would render them (only seen or remembered items, gated by LOS, lighting, and seen-vs-remembered shading), not the raw stack of every in-radius tile
decisive_source: src/arcopolis_export.cpp::write_entities(items) reads get_map().i_at(p) for every point_in_radius inside the export window and emits every raw ground item unconditionally, with no seen/LOS/lighting/memory gating
divergence: An item sitting on a tile behind a wall or in unlit darkness (outside the avatar's LOS) is returned by map::i_at and painted by the snapshot, but the GUI would never display it there because the tile is unseen — producing ghost items the real renderer would never show
